88733a69d4fdfa7d0ce76aa7bb5a263dad520388chore(release): prepare v0.1.0 for npm publishThe package had no license, no CI, no release automation, and
package.json metadata too thin to be installable in good conscience.

the tool's own spec. Add a CI workflow (lint/build/test on Node
20/22/24, plus validating our own CHANGELOG.md) and a release
workflow that publishes to npm with provenance on GitHub release.

0b748be7dd674bcd1d6911acb2baeaf6a6aae25cfeat!: drop platform tokens from the heading tag runPlatform values were living in two places: the heading tag run and
product.platforms/the escape hatch. Collapsing them to the latter
only keeps the run scanning as lifecycle facts (yanked, routine) and
makes platforms/frontmatter the single source of truth, with the
hatch as the per-entry override.

A platform token in a heading is now an unknown tag, not a platform
assignment — heading/unknown-tag fires and the consumer drops the
token. PLATFORM_TAGS/PlatformTag are renamed PLATFORMS/Platform, and
platform-value checking is factored into checkPlatforms, shared by
frontmatter and escape-hatch parsing.

BREAKING CHANGE: a release heading tag run no longer accepts platform
tokens (e.g. `(yanked, linux)`). Use product.platforms or the escape
hatch's `platforms:` key instead; a platform token left in a heading
now reports heading/unknown-tag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet <noreply@anthropic.com>

9cedcf502175cf9bad0aca6a0e0fc04249dbce9efeat!: enforce spec's YAML profile and tighten conformance rulesParsing and validation had drifted from a close reading of the draft
spec; this pass closes those gaps so the tool trusts nothing the
spec doesn't actually license.

- Parse frontmatter and the escape hatch under the failsafe YAML
  profile the spec requires (no anchors, aliases, custom tags, or
  multi-document streams), so unquoted values like `1.10` and dates
  stay strings instead of misparsing as numbers.
- Detach change-item reference tails (issues, CVEs, links, credits)
  into structured `references` instead of discarding them, and
  recognize covered-version attribution (`**2.3.1** — ...`),
  validated against the entry's `covers`.
- Never fall back to a fabricated GitHub-anchor fragment for an
  entry's URL; only `url:`, the heading link, canonical, or
  homepage are trusted.
- Split skipped headings into date-bearing candidates vs. plain
  non-candidates, diagnosing near-misses (unpadded dates, no-break
  spaces, missing seconds/offset) as errors instead of silence.
- Promote duplicate `###` sections, a `routine` release with
  categorized changes, and closed product/document key violations
  to errors; gate version/content agreement on
  `product.versioning: semver` instead of guessing a scheme.
- Redefine Level 2 as a structural scan for stray top-level lists,
  and report addressability and skipped-heading counts alongside
  the level.

BREAKING CHANGE: `SkippedHeading.smellsLikeRelease` is renamed to
`candidate`; `ReleaseEntry.anchor` and `HeadingDate.hasOffset` are
removed; `heading/skipped-release-like` and `heading/offset-missing`
are replaced by `heading/candidate-does-not-parse` (error); several
rule severities changed (`entry/duplicate-section`,
`frontmatter/unknown-key` on `product`/`document`, unresolved
`superseded-by`); entry URLs no longer fall back to a
canonical+anchor fragment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet <noreply@anthropic.com>
